chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! When I die, wash me with seven buckets from the well of Ghars.'

key_terms.بِئْرِ غَرْسٍ: The well of Ghars (a specific well in Medina)
key_terms.سَبْعِ قِرَبٍ: Seven buckets/containers (qirb is a leather water container)
key_terms.غَسِّلْنِي: Wash me (imperative, referring to ritual bath/ghusl)

ai.seo_question: What specific instruction did the Prophet give to Ali regarding his ritual washing after death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s specific preference for the water of Ghars, a well in Medina renowned for its medicinal properties, to be used for his ritual washing (ghusl). It underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s personal sunnah in burial rites and the spiritual significance of using blessed water, reflecting the belief in the physical and spiritual purity of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ali<sup>asws</sup>: ‘O Ali<sup>asws</sup>! When I<sup>saww</sup> pass away, so wash me<sup>saww</sup> with seven buckets from the well of Ghars’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hafs al-Bakhtariy who has said

the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah said to Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, “O Ali, when I die give me Ghusl (bath) with seven pails of water from Ghars well.’””
